newsitem.title: UK: Euro bourses revive, gold steady, oil slips.
newsitem.headline: Euro bourses revive, gold steady, oil slips.

text.p: The London stock market moved back near record levels in early trading on Thursday after weathering a scare over higher interest rates, and other leading European bourses were also close to their peaks.

Recovering from a shaky opening after Wall Street slipped overnight, London shares climbed on news of slower inflation, followed by confirmation that official British interest rates would be held at six percent for now.

Gold, weakened by competition from a firmer dollar and booming stock markets plus concern over central bank gold sales, held its ground after recent falls. But oil declined after a weather-related spike upwards on Wednesday.
On the currency markets, the dollar was steady after what market analysts said was an expected correction following a move above 1.60 marks and a 46-month high against the yen.

"We're seeing a correction after the dollar's rise to 1.60 marks but we don't see that progressing too much further. Similarly, the downside looks fairly limited on the yen," said Ian Gunner, senior economist at Chase Investment Bank.

European bourses had already taken their cue from Wall Street to book some profits on Wednesday after hitting record levels. The Dow Jones industrial average, well into the minus column at the European close, ended 35.41 points lower at 6,726.88, snapping a four-session streak of record finishes.
On balance, economists had not expected a British interest rate rise yet, despite the Bank of England's known desire for higher rates to contain inflationary risks.
But surprisingly strong British jobless data on Wednesday, with unemployment falling to a six-year low, had raised a few doubts and sent shares lower after earlier record levels.

The London stock market, Europe's busiest, opened a little easier on Thursday. But it was then reassured by news that inflation slowed to 2.5 percent last month from November's 2.7 percent and the decision to keep interest rates unchanged.

French stocks, also on interest rate watch, were moderately higher ahead of a Bank of France policy-setting meeting at which dealers and economists said its intervention rate could be trimmed to 3.10 percent from 3.15.
The central bank's monetary council meeting, the first since the appointment of two new members seen to lean more towards faster rate cuts, is due to end at about 1215 GMT.

In Frankfurt, shares were little changed based on the DAX index for floor trade but showed gains on the IBIS DAX index for computerised trade, which had taken into account lower prices on Wednesday afternoon.

Gold was steady around the previous London closing levels but the bullion market remained concerned that other European central banks might follow the example of the Dutch and sell more of their gold reserves, traders said.
"In the coming months and years, European central banks will gradually reduce their gold reserves," one Zurich trader said.
World oil prices, which had recovered in late trade on Wednesday amid concern over cold U.S. weather, eased.
London February futures for international benchmark North Sea Brent blend were down 25 cents at $23.59 a barrel.

Elsewhere, the Bank of Spain made a cut of one-quarter point to six percent in its key money market rate, surprising analysts and dealers despite the peseta's recent strength and good December inflation data. The peseta responded by strengthening to around 83.56 to the mark from 83.70 overnight.
Thursday's diary of statistics includes U.S. weekly jobless claims at 1330 GMT and the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia's business survey at 1500 GMT.
CURRENCIES AT 1030 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 116.95 yen and 1.5885 marks, compared with 117.17 and 1.5912 in late business on Wednesday.
Sterling weakened to 2.6620 marks from 2.6701 overnight.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1030 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of top British shares was up 27.7 points at 4,186.6, compared with Wednesday's all-time high of 4,191.5.
Frankfurt's 30-share DAX was down just 0.22 point at 2,988.23 in floor trade but the IBIS DAX index for electronic trade was up 12.42 at 2,988.98.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 17.79 at 2,405.77.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $354 an ounce, compared with the previous London close of $354.15. Silver was steady at $4.70.
